newsitem.title: MEXICO: Early results show Mexico PRI losing lower house.
newsitem.headline: Early results show Mexico PRI losing lower house.

text.p: Early official results from Mexico's elections on Sunday showed President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) losing control of the lower house of Congress for the first time since the party was founded in 1929.

The preliminary results from the Federal Electoral Institute (IFE), with 10.82 percent of polling stations reporting, showed the PRI with 36.58 percent of the votes, well short of the 42.2 percent it needed for a majority in the lower house under Mexico's complicated electoral system.
The right-wing National Action Party (PAN) had 30.62 percent of the votes, followed by the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) with 23.79 percent.
Other small parties, led by the ecologists with 4.09 percent, had the remainder.
The IFE said it hoped to have a majority of the votes counted by late Sunday night.
